proposals.before: Legend made the xiezhi a one-horned creature that knew justice from injustice; Chu’s kings turned its image into headgear.
proposals.after: Legend made the xiezhi a one-horned creature that knew justice from injustice; the king of Chu once obtained one and therefore made it into a cap.
proposals.reason: Chinese 楚王嘗獲之 is singular and states the king obtained the xiezhi; idiomatic wrongly pluralizes and drops that clause.

proposals.before: Kings of Liu blood wore a red-based four-color ribbon about twenty-one feet long.
proposals.after: Feudal kings wore a red-based four-color ribbon about twenty-one feet long.
proposals.reason: Chinese 諸侯王 does not specify Liu blood; that lineage detail is invented in the idiomatic English.

decisions.reason: Chinese 楚王嘗獲之，故以爲冠 is singular and states that the king of Chu once obtained a xiezhi and therefore made a cap from it; the idiomatic plural 'Chu’s kings' and 'turned its image into headgear' omit the acquisition and invent a plural subject.
Chinese 諸侯王 means feudal kings and does not name the Liu lineage; 'Kings of Liu blood' invents kinship detail absent from the source.
